gap: BHD IS CLEAN, proven with a positive control, so this is a design verdict not leakage. Raw counts vs baseline-*.png with the BHD key forced are large (customer 307,861/5,184,000; invoice 953,283; dashboard 2,438,282; dashboard-390 597,008/1,316,640) but I looked at them: the baseline shows 6 international clients under 'Meridian Supply Group'/'Sam', today's DB has 10 Oman clients under 'COMPANY Name'/'Wave' - and the teal accent, 220px labelled sidebar, UPPERCASE sort-caret headers and outlined Company pills are pixel-identical in position. Stale DATA. The decisive same-session A/B: BHD forced, wave sheet enabled vs disabled = 0 differing px on /invoice, /customer and the dashboard at 1440 and 0 on the dashboard at 390. The identical disable run under the P&P key flips --color-accent #2b57d8 to #009bc1 and changes 2,393,885/5,184,000 px (46.18%), so the mechanism is real and the 0s mean something. The JS half is IS_PNP-gated and confirmed inert under BHD. METHOD NOTE for the next critic: forcing only the data-product attribute is NOT enough. PRODUCT_KEY is read from window.__ERP_PRODUCT at MODULE LOAD, so an attribute-only override leaves IS_PNP false and the whole DataTable.jsx half dead - my first capture measured .wave-col-uniform on 0/10 cells and I nearly reported the uniform-column gate as a 76-line no-op. With window.__ERP_PRODUCT set in an addInitScript it works exactly as documented: Payment (1 distinct value on 10 rows) gets wave-col-uniform on 10/10 cells, drops to #5b6779 weight 400 with the triangle at 0.6, and 10 wave-badge-uniform on the phone; Status (2 distinct values) is untouched. THE DESIGN: this is the closest round yet. /customer at 1440 beats Wave outright (dead-even 72px rows x10 spread 0.0, pale #f1f4f9 non-uppercase header, hairline #e8edf5 rules, no vertical rules, no zebra, one white container, bold #101828 name). On /invoice three of r6's four defects are genuinely fixed: the six KPI cards are de-hued to one border and one ink, the amber 10-of-10 'Evidence Incomplete' is quiet, the Client cell now ellipsises ('Al Manara Integrated Facilities Managemen...'), and font-variant-numeric is tabular-nums. But the money column still does not form a straight edge, and it breaks worst on the largest numbers. MEASURED on Total at 1440: the td content-box right edge is 901px on all ten cells, and the painted right edges are 901 x6, 910.3, 912.9 and 919.4 - four different edges. The amount span is display:inline-flex, so once its content exceeds the cell's content width it OVERFLOWS right instead of shrinking: 123,456.789 hangs 11.9px into the 18px padding and $ 15,420.750 USD hangs 18.4px and lands flush on the cell boundary at 919, touching Paid. The three widest amounts on the page are exactly the three that leave the column. Compounding it, one column carries three notations - OMR rows a leading Rial glyph and no suffix, USD rows a leading '$' AND a trailing 'USD' - and it is that trailing USD that pushes row 6 out. Wave's single number, $25,980.23, sits in a column. A ledger's one job is that decimals line up; this is not taste. Also still louder than the bar: six summary cards plus a caption sentence put the first row at y=360 while five of the six read 0/10 or 0.00% (Wave's equivalent is one selector reading 'All Accounts $25,980.23'); at 390 that strip scrolls horizontally with the third card cut mid-word at the viewport edge and no scroll affordance; the locked 40x40 z-1050 padlock FAB at x338-378 still overlaps the card list, which runs to x366, and _tables.css section 10c openly concedes it and defers it to a file this agent does not own; and two adjacent /invoice controls are both placeholder 'search'. Fix the inline-flex overflow (let the amount shrink, or move the currency mark into a fixed gutter and drop the trailing USD) and this wins.
